A method is provided for forming a three-dimensional object having a desired decoration on its surface. The method uses an apparatus capable of discharging multiple types of ink in a controlled manner so that the object can be built with both a decorative appearance and an internal layered structure that enhances the visual effect of the decoration.

The apparatus includes a reflective ink head, a decorative ink head, and a transparent ink head. The reflective ink head discharges reflective ink for forming a light reflection layer. The decorative ink head discharges decorative ink for forming a decorative layer that provides the desired color, pattern, image, or other visual design. The transparent ink head discharges transparent ink for forming a transparent layer between the decorative layer and the light reflection layer. The apparatus also includes a main-scanning driving unit and a sub-scanning driving unit. The main-scanning driving unit moves the ink heads and the object relative to each other in a main-scanning direction, while the sub-scanning driving unit moves them relative to each other in a sub-scanning direction.

In this apparatus, the decorative ink head and the transparent ink head are arranged so that their positions are offset from each other in the sub-scanning direction. This positional offset allows the apparatus to control the order and timing with which the decorative ink and transparent ink are deposited during formation of the three-dimensional object. As a result, the transparent layer can be accurately formed in a predetermined position relative to the decorative layer.

During formation, the reflective ink head, the transparent ink head, and the decorative ink head cooperate to create a layered structure. The reflective ink is used to form a light reflection layer, the transparent ink is used to form a transparent layer over the light reflection layer, and the decorative ink is used to form a decorative layer over the transparent layer. In this way, the transparent layer is positioned between the light reflection layer and the decorative layer.

The resulting three-dimensional object has a structure in which the decorative layer, the transparent layer, and the light reflection layer are arranged in this order from the surface of the object toward the inner side. Because the light reflection layer is located behind the transparent layer and the decorative layer, light entering from the surface side can pass through the decorative layer and the transparent layer, be reflected by the light reflection layer, and return toward the viewer. This structure can improve the visibility, brightness, and depth of the decoration, thereby enabling the three-dimensional object to exhibit a desired decorative appearance.

A method is provided for forming a decorated three-dimensional object by applying multiple types of ink to the surface of the object with an inkjet-type printing apparatus. The apparatus includes a head for ejecting a light-reflective ink, a head for ejecting a decorative ink, and a head for ejecting a transparent ink. At least the head for ejecting the decorative ink and the head for ejecting the transparent ink are arranged so as to be offset from one another in a sub-scanning direction, allowing the respective inks to be applied to the object in a controlled sequence while the object and the heads are moved relative to each other.

In this method, the inks are deposited on the three-dimensional object so that, when viewed from the outside of the object, a decorative layer is positioned closest to the object surface, a transparent layer is formed beneath the decorative layer, and a light reflection layer is formed beneath the transparent layer. The decorative layer provides a desired image, pattern, color, character, texture, or other visual design. The transparent layer is interposed between the decorative layer and the light reflection layer, thereby contributing depth, gloss, and a sense of transparency to the appearance of the decoration. The light reflection layer reflects light passing through the transparent layer and decorative layer, improving brightness, visibility, and decorative quality.

By using separate heads for the different inks and arranging the heads with an offset in the sub-scanning direction, the apparatus can efficiently form the layered structure on a curved, uneven, or otherwise three-dimensional surface. The sequence of ink deposition can be controlled so that each layer is formed with the appropriate thickness, position, and curing state. As a result, the method enables high-quality decoration of three-dimensional objects, providing a visually enhanced appearance that may include improved brilliance, depth, contrast, and reflectivity compared with decorations formed using only ordinary colored ink.

counterfactuals.prompt: Rewrite this 3D printing invention description in patent-style language, focusing on the apparatus heads for reflective ink, decorative ink, and transparent ink and the resulting layer order.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a three-dimensional printing apparatus comprises a build platform and a printhead assembly movable relative to the build platform in at least one of an X-axis, Y-axis, or Z-axis direction. The printhead assembly includes a plurality of material-deposition heads configured to selectively deposit different printable compositions to form a multi-layer decorative article.

The plurality of material-deposition heads includes a reflective-ink deposition head configured to dispense a reflective ink composition, a decorative-ink deposition head configured to dispense a colored, patterned, or image-forming decorative ink composition, and a transparent-ink deposition head configured to dispense a transparent or substantially transparent ink composition. Each of the reflective-ink deposition head, decorative-ink deposition head, and transparent-ink deposition head may be independently controlled to deposit its respective ink in a predetermined pattern and in a predetermined sequence according to print data.

In operation, the reflective-ink deposition head deposits a reflective ink layer onto a substrate, support surface, or previously formed layer. The decorative-ink deposition head subsequently deposits a decorative ink layer over the reflective ink layer, the decorative ink layer defining at least a portion of a visible graphic, color region, texture, indicia, or ornamental pattern. The transparent-ink deposition head thereafter deposits a transparent ink layer over the decorative ink layer. The transparent ink layer may function as a protective, optical, leveling, gloss-enhancing, or depth-enhancing layer while permitting the decorative ink layer and reflective ink layer to remain visible therethrough.

Accordingly, the resulting printed structure comprises, in order from a lower side toward an exposed viewing side: a reflective ink layer, a decorative ink layer disposed on the reflective ink layer, and a transparent ink layer disposed on the decorative ink layer. The reflective ink layer is positioned beneath the decorative ink layer so as to reflect incident light passing through or interacting with the decorative ink layer, thereby enhancing brightness, contrast, metallic appearance, iridescence, or other visual characteristics of the printed article. The transparent ink layer is positioned above the decorative ink layer to provide an outer light-transmissive surface and to protect or optically modify the underlying decorative and reflective layers.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an apparatus and method for producing a 3D object with a decorative layer, transparent layer, and light reflection layer, using inkjet heads offset in the sub-scanning direction.
counterfactuals.output:
An apparatus for producing a three-dimensional object may be configured to form, on a surface of a 3D base object, a multilayer printed structure including:

1. a decorative layer,
2. a transparent layer, and
3. a light reflection layer,

where the layers are deposited by inkjet heads arranged with positional offsets in a sub-scanning direction.

## Apparatus

The apparatus may include:

- a support or holding unit configured to hold a three-dimensional object;
- a moving mechanism configured to move the object and/or inkjet heads relative to each other in a main scanning direction and a sub-scanning direction;
- a first inkjet head configured to discharge decorative ink;
- a second inkjet head configured to discharge transparent or clear ink;
- a third inkjet head configured to discharge light-reflective ink, such as white ink, metallic ink, silver ink, or ink containing reflective particles;
- a curing unit, such as an ultraviolet light source, configured to cure the discharged inks;
- a controller configured to control ink discharge, scanning, head movement, and curing.

The inkjet heads are arranged so that at least two of the heads are offset from one another in the sub-scanning direction. For example, the decorative ink head, transparent ink head, and reflective ink head may be displaced relative to each other in the sub-scanning direction by predetermined distances. This allows different functional layers to be formed in sequence during repeated scanning passes while maintaining accurate registration between the layers.

## Layer Structure

The printed multilayer structure may be formed on the surface of the 3D object in the following order:

- a light reflection layer formed closest to the object surface;
- a transparent layer formed over the light reflection layer; and
- a decorative layer formed over the transparent layer.

Alternatively, depending on the viewing direction and object design, the decorative layer may be formed first, followed by the transparent layer and then the reflective layer. In a preferred configuration for viewing from the outside, the decorative layer is visible through or on the transparent layer, while the light reflection layer enhances brightness, color saturation, and visual depth.

The transparent layer may function as a spacer layer or optical layer. By separating the decorative layer from the reflective layer, it can produce depth, gloss, stereoscopic appearance, or enhanced decorative effects.

## Method

A method for producing the three-dimensional object may include the following steps:

1. **Holding the object**  
   A 3D object is fixed on a support table, jig, rotary holder, or other holding mechanism.

2. **Relative scanning**  
   The inkjet heads and the object are moved relative to each other in a main scanning direction. After each scan, relative movement is performed in the sub-scanning direction.

3. **Discharging reflective ink**  
   A light reflection layer is formed by discharging reflective ink from a reflective inkjet head onto a target region of the object.

4. **Discharging transparent ink**  
   A transparent layer is formed by discharging clear ink from a transparent inkjet head over the reflective layer. The transparent layer may be built up by multiple passes to obtain a desired thickness.

5. **Discharging decorative ink**  
   A decorative layer is formed by discharging colored decorative ink from one or more decorative inkjet heads according to image data.

6. **Curing**  
   Each layer, or each set of droplets, is cured by a curing unit. The curing may be performed after every pass, after each layer, or after completion of multiple layers.

7. **Repeating layer formation**  
   The scanning, discharge, and curing operations are repeated until the desired multilayer decorative structure is completed.

## Offset Arrangement in the Sub-Scanning Direction

The inkjet heads are not aligned at the same position in the sub-scanning direction. Instead, they are shifted by predetermined intervals. For example:

- the reflective ink head is positioned upstream in the sub-scanning direction;
- the transparent ink head is positioned downstream from the reflective ink head;
- the decorative ink head is positioned further downstream.

Because of this offset arrangement, when the object is advanced in the sub-scanning direction between passes, a region that first receives reflective ink subsequently reaches the transparent ink head and then the decorative ink head. Thus, the three layers can be formed in a controlled order with good positional accuracy.

The controller compensates for the offset distances by adjusting discharge timing and scan data. The offset also reduces interference between freshly deposited inks and enables each layer to be at least partially cured before the next layer is applied.

## Advantages

Such an apparatus and method provide:

- accurate registration of decorative, transparent, and reflective layers;
- improved brightness and color development due to the reflective layer;
- increased depth and gloss due to the transparent layer;
- efficient production because multiple inkjet heads can operate during scanning;
- suitability for curved or irregular 3D surfaces;
- reduced mixing or bleeding between different functional inks;
- decorative effects such as metallic appearance, depth expression, lens-like gloss, or high-saturation color.

In summary, the apparatus uses a plurality of inkjet heads arranged with offsets in the sub-scanning direction to sequentially form a decorative layer, a transparent layer, and a light reflection layer on a three-dimensional object. The method controls relative scanning, ink discharge timing, and curing so that the layers are accurately superposed to create a visually enhanced decorative 3D article.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical summary for a 3D printing method that forms a desired decoration by depositing decorative ink, transparent ink, and reflective ink in order using main and sub-scanning mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output:
A 3D printing method is provided for forming a desired decoration on a target surface by sequentially depositing multiple functional inks using a printing head controlled by a main-scanning mechanism and a sub-scanning mechanism.

The method includes moving an inkjet head relative to a workpiece in a main scanning direction while ejecting decorative ink to form a decoration layer corresponding to a predetermined image or pattern. After or in coordination with the decorative ink deposition, transparent ink is deposited over at least a portion of the decoration layer to form a transparent layer that provides surface thickness, gloss, protection, or optical depth. Reflective ink is then deposited in a selected region, either beneath, above, or adjacent to the transparent layer, to form a reflective layer that enhances brightness, metallic appearance, visibility, or decorative contrast.

The main-scanning mechanism reciprocally moves the inkjet head or the workpiece in the main scanning direction, while the sub-scanning mechanism shifts the relative position between the inkjet head and the workpiece in a sub-scanning direction intersecting the main scanning direction. By repeating main scans and sub-scans, the decorative ink, transparent ink, and reflective ink are accurately deposited at prescribed positions based on print data representing the desired decoration.

In one implementation, the decorative ink is first deposited to define color or image information, the transparent ink is subsequently deposited to build a clear relief or protective coating, and the reflective ink is finally deposited to provide a metallic, mirror-like, glittering, or light-reflecting effect. The deposition order and thickness of each ink may be controlled on a pixel-by-pixel or layer-by-layer basis to produce a three-dimensional decorative structure having improved optical appearance, durability, and design flexibility.

This method enables precise formation of complex decorative effects, including raised clear features, embedded or exposed reflective regions, and multi-layer visual textures, using coordinated main and sub-scanning operations.
